this is how app founders are scaling to $10k/mo with slideshows.

you'll need to spend 4-6 hours on this on just one day, and get content for 2+ months without touching it.

a great format to copy is this:

content, content, content, content, ad warmup, app push

the idea is to make slideshow posts that feel like actual content, then only bring in the app/saas shoutout near the end

so instead of posting obvious ads, the account posts stuff that looks like normal tiktok slideshow content:

lifestyle takes, niche opinions, curiosity hooks, "things nobody tells you," etc. the images on the post are an example

find hundreds of lifestyle/travel/interior-style visuals on pinterest / google

use ai to generate dozens of similar captions that basically say the same thing
sneak the app into the content without making it look too promotional
posting across multiple tiktok accounts
one of my top posts on tiktok got 1.2M views like this: PROOF

i set up a workflow with:

claude code (using terminal. it's actually more powerful than claude app, you don't need to be a dev to use this, just a few scary commands you copy and paste). HIGHLY RECOMMENDED to not skip.

socialclaw (cli tool to schedule to social media. you install via sudo npm install -g socialclaw and claude code can schedule posts for you)
openai api or any other image api (e.g gemini api, any other good image model). we'll need this later.
HERE'S HOW TO SPEND THESE 4-6 HOURS:

0-60 minutes —> research competitors. is your app a note taker? search note taker on tiktok and just view all top posts, screenshot all of them. do NOT SKIP.

keep notes of what they write in captions/text over slides. just copy paste somewhere. save for later.

hour 1 - hour 3 —> go to pinterest. remember those screenshots you took? find similar reference images on pinterest. spend 2 hours doing this.

figure out what slide 1 should look like. figure out what slide 2 should look like. etc.
download a few images for each slide type from pinterest. name them as slide_1_1.jpg etc.

hour 4 —> now, not all pinterest photos are allowed to be reposted.
in that case, ask claude code to see the images and use openai image api to generate 100x copies of those images with slight variations but keeping the same vibe!
now you'll have for example 5 slide types x 100 variations = 500 images. do less to start maybe.

hour 5 —> remember the notes of captions you took? ask claude now to overlay caption variations over all those images and tell it "here are how the captions you generate for our posts should look like [paste caption list from competitors]. copy the best ones".
claude code then:

comes up with slideshow angles

writes the slide-by-slide text
keeps the early slides content-first
adds the app/product later in the slideshow
claude will generate captions and it can actually overlay text over images (that's why i told you to use claude code before). it uses ffmpeg library (like all video/image software) to overlay text automatically.

ask claude to schedule 2x posts a day for each account. after that socialclaw handles the actual posting side:

uploads

-> account handling
-> scheduling
-> publishing

THAT'S IT. YOU'RE DONE. you now have months worth of content, it's all scheduled to be posted.

the reason this is useful is that this strategy is insanely repetitive

10 accounts posting 2x posts a day = 20 posts a day.

90% of posts go under ~5,000 views, most even staying under 300 views.

a few posts on each account get 50K - 500K views (some even 1M+)

format stays the same, just fresh similar content. e.g. same tokyo photo, just a different variation.

0.1-2% of viewers actually download the app depending on your content

multiply this by 30 days and you get plenty of traffic
once the workflow is set up, it becomes much easier to run this like a system instead of making random one off posts.

Not Everything is For Everyone, and that's a Good Thing

The AI good, AI bad debate.
The "people don't read books anymore" panic.
The "Education isn't teaching practical skills" outrage.

The ongoing discontent in these tangential spaces boil down to one core sentiment:

"This good thing, that undeniably is good for society, should be instilled in everyone."

And, consequently,

"Because not everyone possesses, appreciates, or actively partakes this undeniably good thing for society, our civilization is in crisis."

We see this in the explosion of comments too frequently echoed: 
"AI is essential for those who couldn't to finally create art!"
"A post-literacy culture will create a dangerous bifurcation of literati vs the illiterate!"
"Education is not preparing the next generation for jobs and survival!"

I particularly do not understand it when it is the anti-communist, freedom-loving, personal-responsibility touting conservatives that clutch their pearls and gasp in such like fashion.

We have gone from "Of course everyone needs to go to college," realizing that that path doesn't work, promoting alternatives like entrepreneurship and trade skills, to now coming full circle again ---

"Of course everyone should A, B, C!"

Because the thought, once more, since no lesson has been learned, is that an elevated civilization means everyone is intelligent, productive, resourceful, driven ... in THIS particular way, or else DOOM.

I propose that an elevated civilization truly only  needs these basic elements:

1.Accountability Culture.
2.Desire to Strive for Personal Betterment.
3. Looking Up to Godliness.

Foster these, and the rest will take care of itself, in whatever form it will look like, in however it needs to look like.

That extra lift of limit on Grok Imagine?
The beautiful library of physical books?
That state-funded mandatory Home economics class?

Bells and Whistles.

The truth is, America is over-abundant -- everything can be obtained, to a degree of manner, for free, for cheap, and nigh on instantly.

The ones that are creating art, that are sitting brooding over dense great books, the ones that are solving problems... They've been doing it long before it was convenient.

The ones who haven't done so, will not even with a magic spoon.

And those in between? They are doing their thing, in ways unconventional and unfamiliar. 

We need to rein back on the obsession over Democratizing everything under the sun. Not everything is for everyone, and that is a good thing.

Reward-guided diffusion: reinforcement learning steers generative models toward novel, stable crystals

Anyone who trains generative models knows the tension. A diffusion model fit by maximum likelihood learns to reproduce its training distribution, so it samples what looks familiar. In materials discovery, though, the interesting compounds sit in the low-probability tails, the underexplored regions where genuinely new structures live. Sampling more of the same is exactly what you do not want.

Hyunsoo Park and Aron Walsh reframe this as a post-training problem. Instead of nudging outputs with heuristics like classifier-free guidance, they fine-tune the model with reinforcement learning, optimizing explicit rewards rather than data likelihood. The move that makes it tractable: they run diffusion in a compressed VAE latent space, which turns the awkward mix of discrete atom types and continuous coordinates into a homogeneous action space where policy gradients behave.

The engine is GRPO, the same group-relative policy optimization behind recent reasoning LLMs, here driving a denoising diffusion policy. The reward is multi-objective and, crucially, verifiable: a creativity term for uniqueness and novelty, a stability term using a machine-learning force field as a fast proxy for DFT energy above the convex hull, and a diversity term that blocks mode collapse.

The payoff is a clean shift of the Pareto frontier. On the Alex-MP-20 benchmark, their metastable-unique-novel score jumps from 15.9% to 61.3%, novelty climbs from 62.3% to 97.5%, and metastability still rises from 51.2% to 72.1%. Novelty and stability usually trade off, and here RL buys both at once. The same framework handles inverse design too: targeting a 3 eV bandgap, RL keeps chemical validity intact while classifier-free guidance collapses to near-zero.

For discovery pipelines in batteries, catalysis, or semiconductors, the practical takeaway is that a verifiable reward plus policy optimization can redirect a generative model toward candidates worth synthesizing, not merely plausible ones. Swap the reward and the same machinery targets ionic conductivity, formation energy, or a specific gap, giving a modular path from "generates something reasonable" to "generates what the program actually needs."

Paper: Park et al., Nature Machine Intelligence (2026), CC BY 4.0 | https://t.co/4cwgBOxl0F

What if the recipe that let vision pretraining leave contrastive learning behind could work on paired image-text data too - with zero negatives?

LeVLJEPA is the first end-to-end vision-language pretraining method built without negatives. The image embedding predicts the text embedding through a small MLP and vice versa, each matched against a stop-gradient target from the other modality, with a regularizer keeping each modality's embedding distribution close to Gaussian so nothing collapses. No negatives, no temperature, no momentum encoder.

The headline tradeoff: LeVLJEPA is the weakest zero-shot model on ImageNet (42.5% vs SigLIP's 50.8%) - but its dense per-token features are the strongest on frozen-VLM tasks: better GQA, VQAv2, POPE, and segmentation than every contrastive baseline tested.

The provocative reading: on these encoders, zero-shot retrieval and frozen-backbone quality are inversely related. Standard evals measure the property these encoders are no longer deployed for - what matters is the per-token grid the LLM attends over.

A first-of-its-kind open-source video generation model for embodied scenarios, using a Mixture-of-Experts design. 

LingBot-Video from @robbyant_brain, a Diffusion Transformer video foundation model built for embodied AI.

- The flagship 30B model activates only 3B parameters per generation, at 1M-token sequences

- At the same total parameter scale it reaches ~3X the inference efficiency of a Dense architecture at 1M-token sequences (3.18× vs. Dense 30B)

- Aesthetic-only reward models are why video generators fake physics, and this paper basically says so. Physical plausibility is not treated as vibes here; it gets scored through causality, object permanence, non-penetration and material realism.

- The model was not trained only on regular internet videos. Its pretraining data also includes 70,000+ hours of embodied footage, covering robot manipulation, navigation, and first-person action videos, so the model sees examples where movement actually changes the world.

- On RBench, it reports a 0.620 average, ahead of every listed open and closed model, while still losing some columns to Wan 2.6.

RL can't teach an LLM to solve problems it never solves. Robot policies suffer from exactly the same limitation.

The fix turned out to be almost embarrassingly simple: train the policy with diffusion noise during pre-training.

That's it.

The policy covers a much wider action distribution, RL finally has somewhere to search, and we fine-tune VLAs on real robots in under an hour.

Introducing TMRL.
